articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'An Introduction to Software Design Methodologies' (Digest No.129)
publicationTitle: 1992 IEE Colloquium on an Introduction to Software Design Methodologies (Digest No: 1992/129)
1992 IEE Colloquium on an Introduction to Software Design Methodologies (Digest No: 1992/129)
abstract: Jackson System Development is a method that has at its basis the assertion that any computer system is in reality a model of some portion of the real world. The Jackson method is a technical method that is limited to the software life cycle. The author discusses the modelling stage of the Jackson method which is concerned with depicting the subject matter of the system. He considers a case study of a RADAR training simulator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An overview of the HOOD method
publicationTitle: 1992 IEE Colloquium on an Introduction to Software Design Methodologies (Digest No: 1992/129)
abstract: HOOD (Hierarchical Object-Oriented Design) is object-oriented design method which was originally targeted at Ada program development. Object-oriented design approaches are based on identifying the classes of objects in a system. Classes are described in terms of their behaviour and structure, with each object modelling a real-world entity. A class and its operations are defined as a single unit. Each object is a member of a class and the operations are defined for all members of a class. The author provides an overview of HOOD and then looks at some case studies of its application at the European Space Agency and Thorn EMI Electronics. He concludes with a general look at its benefits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A modern approach to the application of Yourdon Structured Methods
publicationTitle: 1992 IEE Colloquium on an Introduction to Software Design Methodologies (Digest No: 1992/129)
abstract: Yourdon Structured Methods provides a fast, flexible and well-defined route to cost-effective production of high-quality software. The author initially discusses the advantages of the Yourdon approach including its flexibility, life-cycle modeling and speed of use. Other issues reviewed include functional decomposition object-oriented analysis and CASE.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: 1992 IEE Colloquium on an Introduction to Software Design Methodologies (Digest No: 1992/129)
abstract: Structured Systems Analysis and Design Method, SSADM, has come of age. System development managers look increasingly to SSADM to be their structured approach to system design. The author discusses the development of SSADM, the development approach, system maintainability, extensibility and portability. He considers SSADM as one of the open methodologies and why it is gaining market share.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: 1992 IEE Colloquium on an Introduction to Software Design Methodologies (Digest No: 1992/129)
abstract: Mascot is a software development method which was originated with clear recognition of the real-life problems of large-scale software creation. It has for the most part attempted to address the problems through pragmatic means by defining a systematic representation of modularity and abstraction, and providing a virtual machine that supports these concepts during development and at run-time. Although not covering the entire development lifecycle. Mascot does provide a framework for what one might term an 'industrial' production of software.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
